case_assessment.summary: The core mechanical accident logic is mostly sound: shell thinning led to shell rupture, and the rupture under hot, pressurized liquid conditions supports the BLEVE consequence. The main gaps are that the graph stops at BLEVE and does not explicitly represent the major toxic atmospheric release consequence, and the BLEVE node evidence is not schema-compliant because it contains paraphrase and commentary rather than a short verbatim quote.
main_problems: The graph captures the vessel-failure/BLEVE path but omits the explicit toxic dispersion consequence from the HF and chlorine release.
The H1 evidence is not a short direct quote; it mixes quotation, paraphrase, and analytical commentary.
The current graph slightly simplifies the scenario by representing multi-chemical reboiler contents primarily through a single HF material node.

node_updates.current_state: Evidence contains a section citation plus paraphrased analysis: "Section 3.2 states: \"Based upon these process conditions at the time of the failure, a BLEVE occurred.\" The incident description explains ... The cause statement further identifies ..."
node_updates.suggested_state: Use a short direct quote only, for example: "Based upon these process conditions at the time of the failure, a BLEVE occurred."
node_updates.reason: The schema requires evidence to be a short quote copied directly from the source. The current evidence field includes non-evidence commentary and paraphrase.
node_updates.evidence: "Based upon these process conditions at the time of the failure, a BLEVE occurred."

node_updates.current_state: The explanation for H1 includes both the BLEVE and the toxic release as part of one consequence description.
node_updates.suggested_state: Clarify that H1 represents the physical pressure-vessel explosion consequence only, while the atmospheric toxic release should be modeled separately as an additional downstream hazard consequence.
node_updates.reason: Separating the physical explosion consequence from the toxic-release consequence improves causal clarity and avoids conflating distinct hazard outcomes.
node_updates.evidence: "Based upon these process conditions at the time of the failure, a BLEVE occurred." and "The contents of the reboiler, the distillation column, and other ancillary equipment were released into the ambient air."

node_additions.reason: A major reported consequence of the rupture was the toxic atmospheric release of HF and chlorine. The current graph ends at BLEVE and misses this important downstream hazard consequence.
node_additions.evidence: "The contents of the reboiler, the distillation column, and other ancillary equipment were released into the ambient air." and "The incident resulted in the release of 871 pounds of HF, 1,684 pounds of chlorine"

issues_summary.description: The graph does not explicitly represent the toxic dispersion consequence from the released HF and chlorine, even though that was a major reported outcome of the rupture.
The BLEVE node evidence is not schema-compliant because it is not a short verbatim quote; it includes paraphrase and analytical text.
The graph simplifies the released process inventory by using only an HF material node, even though chlorine was also a significant released toxic material.
